title: C# 終於有 union types——.NET 11 把 discriminated union 收進型別系統
summary: C# 15 在 .NET 11 preview 2 起引入 union 關鍵字，把 discriminated union 收進語言。它降解成一個自動生成的 struct : IUnion，唯一狀態是 object? Value，由 [Union] attribute 驅動隱式轉換；switch 取得 compiler 的窮舉檢查、漏 case 發 warning。預設 box value type，但可手寫 TryGetValue<T>() 在 hot path 避開 boxing，且消費端程式碼一行不改。純編譯期降解，能 target net8.0 / net48。
widget_questions: When you write `SupportedOS os = new MacOS(...)`, what does the compiler-generated struct hold, which constructor overload fires, and which switch arm matches it — for each of the three union cases?

Which of the four compiler stages (parse the union keyword, generate the struct, lower the implicit conversion, check switch exhaustiveness) owns each step from a one-line union declaration to a not-exhaustive warning, and what does each stage NOT know?

On the construct-once-then-switch path, how does a default-generated union (object? Value, boxes value types) differ from a hand-written union with TryGetValue<T> (stack storage, zero allocation) in storage, GC pressure, and author burden?

As the number of value-type union values constructed per second rises, how far do heap allocation rate and Gen 0 GC frequency diverge between the default boxing union and a hand-written TryGetValue union?

How does the same Result-shaped sum type look across C# 15 union, the OneOf NuGet package, F# discriminated unions, Rust enums, and TypeScript discriminated unions — and where does C#'s warning-not-error exhaustiveness place it?
